Compute the Log-Likelihood Function

Source: R/hllf.R
logLik.Rd

Evaluate a specified model's likelihood, with optional intensity and residual paths.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'hspec'
logLik(
  object,
  inter_arrival,
  type = NULL,
  mark = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  Nc = NULL,
  N0 = NULL,
  Nc0 = NULL,
  lambda_component0 = "auto",
  infer = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An hspec-class object containing parameter values for computing the log-likelihood.

inter_arrival

A vector of inter-arrival times for events across all dimensions, starting with zero.

type

A vector indicating the dimensions, represented by numbers (1, 2, 3, etc.), starting with zero.

mark

A vector of mark (jump) sizes, starting with zero.

N

Optional cumulative event-count matrix, with one row per input row and one column per event type. Each row contains counts after that event.

Nc

Optional cumulative mark-total matrix with the same shape as N.

N0

Initial event counts: a finite scalar or one value per event type. If omitted, use the first row of supplied N, or zero when N is absent.

Nc0

Initial mark totals: a finite scalar or one value per event type. If omitted, use the first row of supplied Nc, or zero when Nc is absent.

lambda_component0

Initial intensity components \(\lambda_{ij}(0)\), excluding the baseline mu. A finite scalar is expanded to every kernel component. A matrix must match the shape of alpha and beta. "auto" (also NULL) selects unconditional component means for supported stable constant numeric linear models, and zero otherwise. "mean" requires supported finite means; "zero" fixes zero components. The selected rule is reported once. Mean initialization excludes nonzero eta, impact callbacks and custom residual distributions. Function-valued core parameters use zero in "auto".

infer

Logical; if TRUE, return intensity paths and residual processes together with the likelihood.

...

Additional arguments passed to or from other methods.

Value

With infer = FALSE, a length-one numeric vector named loglikelihood. With infer = TRUE, a list containing:

  • loglikelihood: the same likelihood value.

  • lambda and rambda: intensity matrices immediately before and after events.

  • lambda_component and rambda_component: the corresponding kernel components, with columns ordered by intensity row, then kernel column.

  • res_process1, ..., res_processD: residuals between successive events of each type. Types with fewer than two events have empty residual vectors.

Intensity matrices include the initial row. For residual-distribution models, res_process values use the specified distribution and eres_process1, ..., eres_processD give their unit-exponential transforms.

Details

The first row represents the initial state and is not an event. Omit type for a univariate model and mark for unit marks. The observation vectors have the same length. The likelihood ends at the last supplied event. Counting-process rows contain values after the corresponding event. Supplied N and Nc matrices must agree with type, mark, and any supplied initial counts. Event order is preserved, including zero intervals. Component functions receive the arguments they declare; functions with ... receive the available event context. Intensity histories are NULL before initialization. Baseline functions use n - 1 to access the preceding event. If initial intensity components are omitted, they are determined from the supplied model. For a fitted model, use fitted_hspec() with the arguments returned by fit_initial_state() to preserve the fit's initialization setting.

With the default automatic selection, standalone logLik() uses the Rcpp engine for numeric Hawkes specifications and parameter-only component functions. These functions have only param as an argument and return plain numeric matrices. Their defaults are evaluated as in the R engine; no Jacobian is required. This supports likelihood values and, with infer = TRUE, intensity paths and residuals. Captured inputs must remain fixed and callbacks must be deterministic. Observed-state impact functions may also use n, N, Nc, marks, types, times and resolved core matrices. They must return finite plain numeric matrices matching the kernel dimensions. Each function retains its own default parameters; standalone evaluation does not apply fitting's sharing rules. Observed baseline functions may use event context, excluding latent intensities, and return finite nonnegative dimensions-by-one matrices. Sequential impacts may explicitly request lambda, lambda_component, or lambda_component_n. They receive the state before the jump. The last post-event intensity uses the next baseline, as in R. Mark densities, residual distributions, unsupported function signatures, and classed numeric inputs use the R engine. rmark and rresidual are simulation generators and do not by themselves prevent numeric likelihood acceleration. Set options(emhawkes.engine = "r") for the R calculation, "auto" for automatic selection, or "cpp" to require a supported specification. Setting "cpp" is not needed for automatic acceleration. The engine supports unequal decay rates within a row and multi-kernel mappings. During fitting, hfit() also supports C++ adapters for the callback models documented there. Engine selection does not change simulation or enable analytic gradients. Automatic capability fallback may evaluate impact callbacks again. User errors propagate; deterministic callbacks with fixed captured inputs are required.
